newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Q1 tax revenues down, below target.
newsitem.headline: German Q1 tax revenues down, below target.

text.p: Total German tax revenues during the first quarter of this year fell by 4.3 percent compared to a year earlier to 170.8 billion marks, government sources said on Tuesday.

The sources said the first three months indicated that tax revenues would fall short of targets this year, but not by as much as the 20 billion marks predicted by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).

Germany's tax take is being closely watched by analysts to see whether Bonn can control its budget deficit sufficiently to qualify for European monetary union this year. A new tax projection for 1997 will be issued next month.

The government's annual economic report in January took into account the impact of a five billion mark shortfall in the final 1996 tax take, and a downward revision in the forecast for nominal growth in gross domestic product this year to 3.5 percent from 3.8 percent, the sources said.
But they added that especially weak revenues from assessed taxes pointed to "limited extra tax shortfalls" this year.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in New York on Tuesday he was optimistic of achieving the Maastricht treaty budget deficit target of three percent of GDP this year.
